- 5 -

Catherine (conquering herself with a mighty effort).
Now self-control. Self-control, Catherine. Philosophy.
Europe is looking on. (She forces herself to sit down.)
Edstaston. Steady, dearest: it is the Empress. Call her
your Imperial Majesty. Call her Star of the North, Little
Mother, Little Darling: that's what she likes; but get the straps
off.
Claire. Keep quiet, dear: I cannot get them off if you move.
Catherine (calmly). Keep quite still, Captain (she tickles
him.)
Edstaston. Ow! Agh! Ahowyow!
Claire (stopping dead in the act of unbuckling the straps
and turning sick with jealousy as she grasps the situation).
Was that what I thought was your being tortured?
Catherine (urbanely). That is the favorite torture of Catherine
the Second, Mademoiselle. I think the Captain enjoys it very
much.
Claire. Then he can have as much more of it as he wants.
I am sorry I intruded. (She rises to go.)
Edstaston (catching her train in his teeth and holding on
like a bull-dog). Don't go. Don't leave me in this horrible
state. Loosen me. (This is what he is saying: but as he says
it with the train in his mouth it is not very intelligible.)
Claire. Let go. You are undignified and ridiculous enough
yourself without making me ridiculous. (She snatches her train
away.)
Edstaston. Ow! You've nearly pulled my teeth out: you're
worse than the Star of the North. (To Catherine.) Darling Little
Mother: you have a kind heart, the kindest in Europe. Have
pity. Have mercy. I love you. (Claire bursts into tears.)
Release me.
Catherine. Well, just to show you how much kinder a Russian
savage can be than an English one (though I am sorry to say I
am a German) here goes! (She stoops to loosen the straps.)
Claire (jealously). You needn't trouble, thank you. (She
pounces on the straps: and the two set Edstaston free between
them.) Now get up, please; and conduct yourself with some
dignity if you are not utterly demoralized.
Edstaston. Dignity! Ow! I can't. I'm stiff all over.
I shall never be able to stand up again. Oh Lord! how it hurts!
(They seize him by the shoulders and drag him up.) Yah! Agh!
Wow! Oh! Mmmmmm! Oh, Little Angel Mother, don't ever do this
to a man again. Knout him; kill him; roast him; baste him;
head, hang, and quarter him; but don't tie him up like that and
tickle him.
Catherine. Your young lady still seems to think that you enjoyed
it.
Claire. I know what I think. I will never speak to him
again. Your Majesty can keep him, as far as I am concerned.
Catherine. I would not deprive you of him for worlds;
though really I think he's rather a darling (she pats his cheek).
Claire (snorting). So I see, indeed.
Edstaston. Don't be angry, dearest: in this country every-
body's a darling. I'll prove it to you. (To Catherine.) Will
your Majesty be good enough to call Prince Patiomkin?
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

叶卡捷琳娜（努力克制自己）。
现在要自制。自制，叶卡捷琳娜。哲学。
欧洲在看着呢。（她强迫自己坐下。）
埃德斯塔斯顿。稳住，亲爱的：这是女皇。称她为陛下。称她为北极星，小妈妈，小宝贝：那是她喜欢的；但先把带子解开。
克莱尔。安静点，亲爱的：你动的话我解不开。
叶卡捷琳娜（平静地）。完全别动，上尉（她挠他痒痒。）
埃德斯塔斯顿。哎哟！啊！啊嚎哟！
克莱尔（在解带子的动作中突然停住，明白情况后嫉妒得感到恶心）。
那就是我以为你在受折磨的事吗？
叶卡捷琳娜（彬彬有礼地）。那是叶卡捷琳娜二世最喜欢的折磨方式，小姐。我想上尉非常享受。
克莱尔。那他想要多少就给他多少吧。
抱歉我闯了进来。（她起身要走。）
埃德斯塔斯顿（用牙齿咬住她的裙摆，像斗牛犬一样死死不放）。别走。别把我留在这种可怕的状态中。松开我。（他嘴里咬着裙摆说这些话，所以听不太清楚。）
克莱尔。松口。你自己已经够没尊严、够可笑的了，别再让我出丑。（她猛地夺回裙摆。）
埃德斯塔斯顿。哎哟！你差点把我的牙拔出来：你比北极星还坏。（对叶卡捷琳娜说。）亲爱的小妈妈：你有一颗善良的心，欧洲最善良的心。可怜可怜我吧。慈悲为怀。我爱你。（克莱尔突然哭了起来。）
放开我。
叶卡捷琳娜。好吧，只是为了向你展示，一个俄罗斯野蛮人能比一个英国野蛮人仁慈多少（虽然很遗憾我是德国人），这就来！（她弯腰去松带子。）
克莱尔（嫉妒地）。不用麻烦你了，谢谢。（她扑向带子：两人一起解开了埃德斯塔斯顿。）现在请起来；如果你还没有彻底丧失士气，就表现得有点尊严。
埃德斯塔斯顿。尊严！哎哟！我做不到。我全身僵硬。
我再也没法站起来了。哦，天哪！多疼啊！
（他们抓住他的肩膀，把他拖起来。）呀！啊！哇！哦！嗯嗯嗯嗯！哦，小天使妈妈，别再对人做这种事了。鞭打他；杀死他；烤了他；浇油烧他；斩首、绞刑、分尸；但别那样把他绑起来挠痒痒。
叶卡捷琳娜。你的年轻女士似乎仍然认为你很享受。
克莱尔。我知道我在想什么。我再也不跟他说话了。至于我，陛下可以留下他。
叶卡捷琳娜。我绝不会夺走他，尽管我真的觉得他挺可爱的（她拍拍他的脸颊）。
克莱尔（哼了一声）。我看出来了，确实。
埃德斯塔斯顿。别生气，亲爱的：在这个国家，每个人都是宝贝。我来证明给你看。（对叶卡捷琳娜说。）陛下能否好心叫一下波将金亲王？

page_data.en:
- 6 -
Catherine (surprised into haughtiness). Why?
Edstaston. To oblige me.
Catherine laughs good-humoredly and goes to the curtains
and opens them. The band strikes up a Redowa.
Catherine (calling imperiously). Patiomkin! (The music
stops suddenly.) Here! To me! Go on with your music there,
you fools. (The Redowa is resumed.)
The sergeant rushes from the ballroom to relieve the Empress
of the curtain. Patiomkin comes in dancing with Varinka.
Catherine (to Patiomkin). The English captain wants you,
little darling.
Catherine resumes her seat as Patiomkin intimates by a grotesque
bow that he is at Edstaston's service. Varinka passes behind
Edstaston and Claire, and posts herself or Claire's right.
Edstaston. Precisely. (To Claire.) You observe, my love:
"little darling." Well, if her Majesty calls him a darling, is
it my fault that she calls me one too?
Claire. I don't care: I don't think you ought to have done
it. I am very angry and offended.
Edstaston. They tied me up, dear. I couldn't help it.
I fought for all I was worth.
The sergeant (at the curtains). He fought with the strength
of lions and bears. You knows I shall carry a broken sweetheart
to my grave.
Edstaston. You can't mean to throw me over, Claire.
(Urgently.) Claire. Claire.
Varinka (in a transport of sympathetic emotion, pleading
with clasped hands to Claire). Oh, sweet little angel lamb,
he loves you: it shines in his darling eyes. Pardon him, pardon
him.
Patiomkin (rushing from the Empress's side to Claire and
falling on his knees to her). Pardon him, pardon him, little
cherub! little wild duck! little star! little glory! little
jewel in the crown of heaven!
Claire. This is perfectly ridiculous.
Varinka (kneeling to her). Pardon him, pardon him, little
delight, little sleeper in a rosy cradle.
Claire. I'll do anything if you'll only let me alone.
The sergeant (kneeling to her). Pardon him, pardon him,
lest the mighty man bring his whip to you. God knows we all
need pardon!
Claire (at the top of her voice). I pardon him! I pardon him!
Patiomkin (springing up joyfully and going behind Claire, whom
he raises in his arms). Embrace her, victor of Bunker's Hill.
Kiss her till she swoons.
The sergeant. Receive her in the name of the holy Nicholas.
Varinka. She begs you for a thousand dear little kisses all
over her body.
Claire (vehemently). I do not. (Patiomkin throws her into
Edstaston's arms.) Oh! (The pair, awkward and shamefaced,
recoil from one another, and remain utterly inexpressive.)
Catherine (pushing Edstaston towards Claire). There is no
help for it, Captain. This is Russia, not England.
Edstaston (plucking up some geniality, and kissing Claire
ceremoniously on the brow). I have no objection.
page_data.zh:
- 6 -
叶卡捷琳娜（惊讶之余变得傲慢）。为什么？
埃德斯塔斯顿。为了成全我。
叶卡捷琳娜和蔼地笑了笑，走到帘子前拉开它们。乐队奏起雷多瓦舞曲。
叶卡捷琳娜（威严地呼唤）。波将金！（音乐突然停止。）过来！到我这里来！你们那些傻瓜，继续演奏。（雷多瓦舞曲重新开始。）
中士从舞厅冲过来，替女皇撩起帘子。波将金跳着舞，带着瓦林卡进来。
叶卡捷琳娜（对波将金说）。这位英国上尉需要你，小宝贝。
波将金做了一个滑稽的鞠躬，表示听从埃德斯塔斯顿的差遣，叶卡捷琳娜随即回到座位上。瓦林卡从埃德斯塔斯顿和克莱尔身后走过，站在克莱尔的右侧。
埃德斯塔斯顿。正是如此。（对克莱尔说。）你注意到了吗，亲爱的：“小宝贝。”好吧，如果陛下叫他宝贝，那她叫我宝贝难道是我的错吗？
克莱尔。我不在乎：我觉得你不该那样做。我很生气，也很 offended。
埃德斯塔斯顿。是他们把我绑起来的，亲爱的。我没办法。我已经尽力反抗了。
中士（在帘子处）。他像狮子和熊一样奋力搏斗。你知道的，我将带着破碎的心进入坟墓。
埃德斯塔斯顿。你不会真的想抛弃我吧，克莱尔。（急切地。）克莱尔。克莱尔。
瓦林卡（充满同情的激动情绪，双手合十向克莱尔求情）。哦，甜蜜的小天使羔羊，他爱你：这在他亲爱的眼睛里闪耀。原谅他，原谅他。
波将金（从女皇身边冲到克莱尔面前，跪在她面前）。原谅他，原谅他，小天使！小野鸭！小星星！小荣耀！天国皇冠上的小宝石！
克莱尔。这简直荒谬透顶。
瓦林卡（跪在她面前）。原谅他，原谅他，小快乐，睡在玫瑰色摇篮里的小宝宝。
克莱尔。只要你们别烦我，我什么都愿意做。
中士（跪在她面前）。原谅他，原谅他，免得那位大力士把鞭子挥向你。天知道我们都需要宽恕！
克莱尔（高声喊道）。我原谅他！我原谅他！
波将金（高兴地跳起来，走到克莱尔身后，将她抱起）。拥抱她吧，邦克山战役的胜利者。吻她直到她昏厥。
中士。以圣尼古拉的名义接受她。
瓦林卡。她请求你在她身上亲上一千个亲爱的小吻。
克莱尔（激烈地）。我没有。（波将金把她扔进埃德斯塔斯顿的怀里。）哦！（两人笨拙且羞愧地互相退缩，完全面无表情。）
叶卡捷琳娜（将埃德斯塔斯顿推向克莱尔）。没办法了，上尉。这里是俄罗斯，不是英国。
埃德斯塔斯顿（鼓起一些亲切感，仪式性地亲吻克莱尔的额头）。我没意见。

page_data.en:
- 7 -

Varinka (disgusted). Only one kiss! and on the forehead!
Fish. See how I ki c, though it is only my horribly ugly old
uncle (she throws her arms round Patiomkin's neck and covers
his face with kisses).
The sergeant (moved to tears). Sainted Nicholas: bless your
lambs!
Catherine. Do you wonder now that I love Russia as I love
no other place on earth?
Naryshkin (appearing at the door). Majesty: the model
for the new museum has arrived.
Catherine (rising eagerly and making for the curtains). Let
us go. I can think of nothing but my museum. (In the archway
she stops and turns to Edstaston, who has hurried to lift the
curtain for her.) Captain, I wish you every happiness that your
little angel can bring you. (For his ear alone.) I could have
brought you more; but you did not think so. Farewell,
Edstaston (kissing her hand, which, instead of releasing, he
holds caressingly and rather patronizingly in his own). I feel
your Majesty's kindness so much that I really cannot leave you
without a word of plain wholesome English advice.
Catherine (snatching her hand )
away and bounding forward as if )
he had touched her with a spur). )
Advice!!! )
Patiomkin. Madman. take ) (Exclaiming simultaneously).
care! )
Naryshkin. Advice the )
Empress!! )
The sergeant. Sainted )
Nicholas! )
Varinka. Hoo hoo! (a )
stifled splutter of laughter). )

Edstaston (following the Empress and resuming kindly but
judicially). After all, though your Majesty is of course a
great queen, yet when all is said, I am a man; and your Majesty
is only a woman.
Catherine. Only a wo - (she chokes).
Edstaston (continuing). Believe me, this Russian extravagance
will not do. I appreciate as much as any man the warmth of
heart that prompts it; but it is overdone; it is hardly in
the best taste: it is - really I must say it - it is not proper.
Catherine (ironically, in German). So!
Edstaston. Not that I cannot make allowances. Your Majesty
has, I know, been unfortunate in your experience as a married
woman -
Catherine (furious). Alle Wetter!!!
Edstaston (sentimentally). Don't say that. Don't think of
him in that way. After all, he was your husband; and whatever
his faults may have been, it is not for you to think unkindly
of him.
Catherine (almost bursting). I shall forget myself.
Edstaston. Come! I am sure he really loved you; and you
truly loved him.
Catherine (controlling herself with a supreme effort). No
page_data.zh:
- 7 -

瓦林卡（厌恶地）。只亲一下！还是亲在额头上！
费什。看我怎么亲，虽然他只是我那丑得吓人的老叔叔（她双臂环住波将金的脖子，满脸亲吻）。
中士（感动得流泪）。圣尼古拉：保佑你们的羔羊！
叶卡捷琳娜。你现在明白我为什么爱俄罗斯，胜过爱世上任何其他地方了吗？
纳雷什金（出现在门口）。陛下：新博物馆的模型送到了。
叶卡捷琳娜（急切起身，走向帘幕）。我们走吧。我心里除了我的博物馆，什么也想不了。（在拱门处她停下脚步，转身面向埃德斯塔顿，后者已急忙上前为她掀起帘子。）上尉，愿你的小天使带给你一切幸福。（仅对他耳语。）我本可以给你带来更多；但你并不这么想。再见了，埃德斯塔顿（吻她的手，他非但没有松开，反而带着爱意且略显屈尊俯就的姿态将其握在自己手中）。我对陛下的善意感激涕零，实在不能不留下一句朴实而有益的英式忠告便离去。
叶卡捷琳娜（猛地抽回手，仿佛被他用马刺踢了一下般向前一跃）。
忠告！！！
波将金。疯子，小心！（同时惊呼）。
纳雷什金。给女皇忠告！！
中士。圣尼古拉！
瓦林卡。呵呵！（压抑住的噗嗤笑声）。

埃德斯塔顿（跟随女皇，语气和蔼但带有评判意味）。毕竟，虽然陛下当然是一位伟大的女王，但归根结底，我是个男人；而陛下只是个女人。
叶卡捷琳娜。只是个女——（她哽咽住）。
埃德斯塔顿（继续说道）。请相信，这种俄式的放纵是不行的。我和任何人一样欣赏促成这种行为的内心热情；但这做得过头了；实在不太高雅：这——我真的必须说——这是不体面的。
叶卡捷琳娜（讽刺地，用德语）。是吗！
埃德斯塔顿。倒不是说我不能体谅。我知道，陛下在作为已婚妇女的经历中一直不幸——
叶卡捷琳娜（愤怒地）。天哪！！！
埃德斯塔顿（感伤地）。别这么说。别那样想他。毕竟，他是你的丈夫；无论他有什么缺点，你都不该对他心存恶念。
叶卡捷琳娜（几乎爆发）。我要失态了。
埃德斯塔顿。得了！我确信他真心爱你；你也真心爱他。
叶卡捷琳娜（极力克制自己）。不

page_data.en:
- 8 -

Catherine. What would Voltaire say?
Edstaston. Oh, never mind that vile scoffer. Set an example
to Europe, Madam, by doing what I am going to do. Marry again.
Marry some good man who will be a strength and support to your
old age.
Catherine. My old - (she again becomes speechless).
Edstaston. Yes: we must all grow old, even the handsomest
of us.
Catherine (sinking into her chair with a gasp). Thank you.
Edstaston.
Edstaston. You will thank me more when you see your little
ones round your knee, and your man there by the fireside in the
winter evenings - by the way, I forgot that you have no fireside
here in spite of the coldness of the climate; so shall I say
by the stove?
Catherine. Certainly, if you wish. The stove by all means.
Edstaston (impulsively). Ah, Madam, abolish the stove: believe
me, there is nothing like the good old open grate. Home!
duty! happiness! they all mean the same thing; and they all
flourish best on the drawingroom hearthrug. (Turning to Claire.)
And now, my love, we must not detain the Queen: she is anxious
to inspect the model of her museum, to which I am sure we wish
every success.
Claire (coldly). I am not detaining her.
Edstaston. Well, goodbye (wringing Patiomkin's hand),
goo-oo-oodbye, Prince: come and see us if ever you visit
England. Spire View, Deepdene, Little Mugford, Devon, will always
find me. (To Varinka, kissing her hand.) Goodbye, Mademoiselle:
goodbye, Little Mother, if I may call you that just once. (Varinka
puts up her face to be kissed.) Eh? No, no, no, no: you don't
mean that, you know. Naughty! (To the sergeant.) Goodbye,
my friend. You will drink our healths with this (tipping him).
The sergeant. The blessed Nicholas will multiply your fruits,
Little Father.
Edstaston. Goodbye, goodbye, goodbye, goodbye, boodbye, goodbye.
He goes out backwards, bowing, with Claire curtseying, having
been listened to in utter dumbfoundedness by Patiomkin and
Naryshkin, in childlike awe by Varinka, and with quite inexpressible
feelings by Catherine. When he is out of sight she rises with
clenched fists and raises her arms and her closed eyes to Heaven.
Patiomkin, rousing himself from his stupor of amazement, springs
to her like a tiger, and throws himself at her feet.
Patiomkin. What shall I do to him for you? Skin him alive?
Cut off his eyelids and stand him in the sun? Tear his tongue
out? What shall it be?
Catherine (opening her eyes). Nothing. But on, if I could
only have had him for my -for my-for my-
Patiomkin (in a growl of jealousy). For your lover?
Catherine (with an ineffable smile). No: for my museum.
page_data.zh:
- 8 -

叶卡捷琳娜。伏尔泰会怎么说？
埃德斯塔顿。哦，别管那个卑鄙的嘲讽者。夫人，请效仿我将要做的事，为欧洲树立榜样。再婚吧。嫁给一个能在你晚年成为依靠和支持的好男人。
叶卡捷琳娜。我的晚——（她再次说不出话来）。
埃德斯塔顿。是的：我们终将老去，即使是我们当中最英俊的人。
叶卡捷琳娜（气喘吁吁地跌坐进椅子里）。谢谢你。
埃德斯塔顿。
埃德斯塔顿。当你看到孩子们围在你膝边，冬夜里有你的男人守在炉火旁时，你会更感谢我——顺便说一句，我忘了这里尽管气候寒冷却没有壁炉；那么我说守在火炉旁好吗？
叶卡捷琳娜。当然，如果你愿意的话。务必说是火炉旁。
埃德斯塔顿（冲动地）。啊，夫人，废除那火炉吧：相信我，没有什么比得上古老而美好的开放式壁炉。家！责任！幸福！它们都意味着同一件事；而且它们在客厅的壁炉地毯上最为兴盛。（转向克莱尔。）现在，亲爱的，我们不能耽搁女王了：她急于去视察她的博物馆模型，对此我们无疑祝愿其圆满成功。
克莱尔（冷淡地）。我没有耽搁她。
埃德斯塔顿。好吧，再见（紧握波将金的手），再——见，亲王：若你有朝一日访问英国，请来探望我们。德文郡小芒福德迪普丁斯派尔维尤府总能找到我。（对瓦林卡，吻她的手。）再见，小姐：再见，“小母亲”，如果我可以这样称呼你一次的话。（瓦林卡仰起脸准备接受亲吻。）呃？不，不，不，不：你不是这个意思，你知道的。淘气！（对中士。）再见，我的朋友。请用这个为我们的健康干杯（给他小费）。
中士。受祝福的尼古拉会使您的果实倍增，小神父。
埃德斯塔顿。再见，再见，再见，再见，拜拜，再见。
他倒退着鞠躬走出门外，克莱尔行屈膝礼相随；波将金和纳雷什金听得目瞪口呆，瓦林卡怀着孩童般的敬畏，而叶卡捷琳娜则怀着难以言喻的情感。待他身影消失，她攥紧拳头站起身，举起双臂，闭目向天。
波将金从惊愕的呆滞中回过神来，如猛虎般扑向她，跪倒在她脚前。
波将金。我要为您对他做什么？活剥他的皮？割下他的眼皮让他在太阳底下站着？撕掉他的舌头？要怎么做？
